# 🏈 How Important is Drafting?

I wanted to find out how much the draft impacts fantasy football success — and which players **delivered the most value** in last season’s draft in order to build a draft board for this upcoming season. Using data from a Fantasy API built of ESPN's private API, draft results from my league, and average draft positions (adp) from Fantasy Pros, I analyzed if the draft really matters and who met or exceeded expectations.

---

## 📊 How I Got the Data

To conduct this analysis, I pulled:
- The full draft order
- Fantasy points scored
- Positional ranks

I also pulled average draft position(adp) from the website fantasy pros at this URL:
https://www.fantasypros.com/nfl/adp/overall.php

This data combines adp from different fantasy sites, creating one number we can can treat as their "market value".

From there, I calculated a custom **Value Over Replacement Player (VORP)** metric based on my league format:

- 14 teams
- 2 RB, 2 WR, 1 TE, 1 Flex (WR/RB/TE), 1 QB, 1 Kicker, 1 D/ST

> **VORP = Player Points − Avg. Starter at Position**

This was usually calculated by getting the next 3-4 players at each position who are treated as the waiver wire/bench players. 

---

## 📈 Correlation Between VORP and Final Standings

The first step was to measure whether average draft VORP correlates with league success. As shown in the chart below, there's a **moderate negative correlation** (r = –0.51), meaning that the **higher your team’s average VORP, the better you tend to finish**.

## 📊 Average VORP by Team

To further illustrate the relationship, I plotted the average VORP per team. Teams with higher average VORP clearly finished higher in the standings. There are some outliers like "The Ralph Dudes" who finished 7th but had the 3rd best draft according to VORP. The second worst draft which was by "Deb's Debsters" led the team to finishing 6th overall, above the average in this 14 team league.

![Bar chart showing average VORP by team](charts/avg_vorp.png)

---
## 📌 VORP by Position

I wanted to see which positions offered the most value. This chart shows the total VORP by position. This is a sum of all starting players at their position to see who adds the most value. Based on the graph, WR's add the most value followed by RB's and QB's. 

![Bar chart of total VORP by position](charts/vorp_by_pos.png)

## 🎯 Draft Pick vs. VORP

There is at least some relationship between how well you draft and how well you perform, but all draft picks are not created equal. At a certain point, drafting becomes useless as you can typically get a player just as good off the waiver wire. To see where that point was I found the correlation between where a player was drafted and their VORP. At around round 8 pick 2, the VORP values become negative, meaning they are likely not going to be starters and easily replaceable. The first 7 rounds are what really matter. It doesn't make sense to draft a position with a negative VORP like a D/ST or K within those first 7 rounds, which follows typical conventions. Even TE's add little after the 7th round so if you want a solid option, your best bet is to choose it before then.

![Bar chart of draft pick vs. VORP](charts/draft_pick_vs_vorp.png)

## 🧾 Conclusion

This analysis shows that the **draft is absolutely critical** to fantasy football success — especially in the first **7 rounds**, where the majority of value is concentrated.

### 🔑 Key Takeaways:
- **Drafting well matters**: higher team VORP correlates with better final standings.
- **Reaches can backfire**, but some bold picks pay off.
- **Steals in late rounds** can be league-winners.
- **Use VORP** to normalize cross-position value and build smarter draft boards.

Whether you're a casual player or a competitive fantasy manager, integrating this kind of analysis into your draft strategy gives you a serious edge.
